title: 2002 HMMT February Team Problem 1
statement: Determine the number of palindromes that are less than 1000 .

solutions.text: Every one-digit number (there are nine) is a palindrome. The two-digit palindromes have the form \(\underline{a} \underline{a}\) for a nonzero digit \(a\), so there are nine of them. A three-digit palindrome is \(\underline{a} \underline{b} \underline{a}\) with \(a\) a nonzero digit and \(b\) any digit, so there are \(9 \times 10=90\) of these. Thus the number of palindromes less than 1000 is \(9+9+90=\mathbf{1 0 8}\).
